title: KV stripe scheduler for hierarchical GPU memory domains (topology-aware sharding)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: design and implement a topology-aware KV cache shard scheduler that treats the cluster of GPUs as hierarchical memory domains (local GPU DRAM, NVLink peer domain, PCIe host spill) and integrates seamlessly with continuous batching and pipeline/tensor parallel runtime. We want lower tail latency for short requests, predictable memory usage across GPUs, and better unit-cost through adaptive replication and prefetching of hot KV slices. This ticket covers protocol design, allocator changes, runtime hooks for batching windows, and a canary rollout in Dedicated clusters.
technical_design: Summary: introduce a Stripe Scheduler that assigns KV key ranges (slices) to shards with three core concepts: (1) hierarchical domains: local, peer (NVLink/PCIE fabric within a node or across nodes), and remote (host/SSD); (2) lease-based ownership with soft replication for hot slices to avoid cross-device stalls; (3) batching-aware prefetch hints integrated into the continuous-batching coordinator so prefetches are amortized across concurrent requests. Allocation: per-GPU slab allocators track slice residency and an async compaction worker consolidates under-utilized slabs. Eviction: LRU+heatmap where hot keys can be soft-replicated to adjacent NVLink peers for read-heavy workloads; full migration occurs during low-load windows. Consistency: leases expire after configured TTL; reads can fall back to remote fetch path which increments locality score; locality score drives adaptive replication. Interaction with parallelism: tensor-parallel shards keep KV shards colocated with model shards when feasible; pipeline stages will prefer local KV for their sequence windows, otherwise use prefetch or lightweight proxy fetch. Metrics: per-slice hitrate, cross-device fetch rate, average lease contention, prefetch success within batching window. Telemetry and counters are exposed to Console for rollout monitoring.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Scheduler places >85% of active slices on local or NVLink peer domains for our benchmark assembly-line workloads at target sequence lengths.
2) 99th percentile generation latency for single-turn requests improves or remains steady compared to baseline when load is up to 70% of capacity.
3) Memory footprint across GPUs stays within 10% of target allocation after adaptive resizing.
4) No data correctness regressions in KV lookup under tensor+pipeline parallel configs.
5) Automated canary rollout and rollback hooks in runtime have been exercised in staging and documented.
implementation_plan:
Milestones:
- Design review and simulation (2 weeks): static topology simulator to validate stripe placements and lease protocol.
- Runtime prototype (3 weeks): implement stripe scheduler, per-GPU slab allocator changes, and lease manager.
- Integration with continuous-batching coordinator (1 week): add prefetch hint API and amortization logic.
- Testing & benchmarks (1 week): end-to-end tests for correctness, performance, and cost.
- Canary rollout in Dedicated (1 week): staged rollout with telemetry dashboards and rollback policy.
Deliverables: RFC doc, runtime PRs, e2e benchmark suite, dashboard tiles for hitrate/latency/replication.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: lease-based ownership could increase cross-device churn under pathological hotkey patterns. Mitigation: implement exponential backoff for lease giveaways and cap soft-replication count per slice.
Risk: prefetching may allocate memory for keys that are never used, increasing OOM risk. Mitigation: budget prefetches using adaptive allocation tied to batching throughput and evict low-locality cold slices.
Risk: interactions with tensor-parallel placement could cause model shard and KV slice divergence. Mitigation: priority affine placement: when creating a model shard we query scheduler affinity and bias slice placement to colocate with tensor shards when it reduces cross-device fetches.
Risk: rollout causing SLO regressions. Mitigation: include automatic rollback on latency or error-rate thresholds and stepwise traffic ramp.
progress_updates: 2026-01-30: Design review completed with Runtime and Research. Decided on lease TTL of 200ms initial value and soft-replica cap=2.
2026-02-10: Static topology simulator shows 78% of active slices colocated on local/NVLink domain for baseline placement; adjusted affinity scoring to prefer NVLink peers within same host.
2026-02-24: Prototype stripe scheduler merged to experimental branch. Basic per-GPU slab allocator implemented; compaction worker still pending.
2026-03-06: Integrated prefetch hint API with continuous-batching coordinator; end-to-end smoke tests passing on single-node staging; starting multi-node perf runs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler logic and lease expiration; integration tests across tensor/pipeline parallel topologies; chaos test to simulate NVLink flaps and remote fetch fallbacks; synthetic workload: assembly-line short-turn workload and long-context scoring workload; performance tests measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost per request. Use same benchmark harness as runtime-2.3 stability tests and record baselines.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge to canary branch behind feature flag. 2) Run canary on 5 Dedicated clusters with low-traffic customer-like workloads. 3) Monitor Console tiles for hitrate, cross-device fetch rate, 99th-latency. 4) Ramp to 25% capacity with automated rollback triggers. 5) Full rollout if metrics stable for 72 hours. Rollback plan includes reverting feature flag and draining leases gracefully by letting TTLs expire and forcing migrations to baseline placement.
notes: This approach differs from previous slab-only sharding by introducing explicit topology domains and a lease/soft-replication protocol to reduce synchronous cross-device fetches in the critical path. It aims to be conservative on memory while allowing adaptive replication for heavy hitters. Follow-up work may expand to NVSwitch-aware clustering and host-level SSD tiering for cold KV slices.
